description: Compare a fixed list of ten security-relevant response headers across two releases and name the specific reverts. Reports a header removed, added or changed, and separately a reduced Strict-Transport-Security max-age, dropped includeSubDomains, a newly permitted unsafe-inline or unsafe-eval, and a Content-Security-Policy that moved from enforcing to report-only so it no longer blocks anything. Observable differences only, not an assessment of whether either configuration is adequate. Pay 110000 atomic USDC on Base via exact x402. MCP does not pay; it provides a challenge handoff.

after.description: Headers from the later release. Names are compared case-insensitively, as HTTP defines them. A repeated header may be an array or a comma-joined string. A header that is absent is omitted; a null value is refused rather than read as present. At most 200 entries.

after_name.description: A label for the later set.

before.description: Headers from the earlier release. Names are compared case-insensitively, as HTTP defines them. A repeated header may be an array or a comma-joined string. A header that is absent is omitted; a null value is refused rather than read as present. At most 200 entries.

before_name.description: A label for the earlier set, such as a release tag, used in the findings.

name: security_header_diff

complete.description: Whether everything supplied was examined. False means part of it was not, which is a different problem from something that is wrong.

finding_count.description: The true total, even when the listing is bounded.

headers.description: Per compared header: its value on each side and whether it changed. The list compared is fixed and published, so a header outside it is not silently ignored.

passed.description: The same verdict under the name shared across the caller-supplied families.

request_id.description: Delivery request identifier; also returned in x-foundry-request-id.

unchanged.description: True only when every compared header was identical. Not a judgement that either configuration is appropriate.

title: Security Header Diff
